title: Azure AI Search ACL and RBAC scopes
summary: Preview as of 2026-10-13: permission fields on the index (userIds, groupIds, rbacScope) are enforced at query time from the user's Entra token, with Microsoft Graph expanding group membership.
useIf: Content is in ADLS Gen2, Blob or SharePoint with Entra identities, preview is acceptable and you want to avoid writing group-expansion code.
avoidIf: You need GA, a non-Entra identity system, deny rules or revocation faster than your sync can deliver.

explain.title: Preview, checked 2026-10-13
explain.md: Native ACL and RBAC scope enforcement needs a preview REST API or SDK (latest preview `2026-08-01-preview`, latest stable `2026-04-01`) [[r18]]. Preview features carry no SLA and are not recommended for production by the docs [[r11]].

The index sets `permissionFilterOption: enabled` and has up to one `filterable` field per permission type: `userIds`, `groupIds` and `rbacScope`. Use Entra object ids (GUIDs), not UPNs or emails. Special values are `"all"` for public and `"none"` [[r15]]. At query time the app sends the user's Entra token in the `x-ms-query-source-authorization` header. Two checks run: the calling app needs Search Index Data Reader (or Contributor), and the user's `oid` and group ids are matched against document ACLs. A document passes if **any** of userIds, groupIds or rbacScope matches [[r12]].

explain.title: Query-time enforcement
explain.alt: The app sends the query with the user's token. Search asks Microsoft Graph to expand group membership, filters documents by ACL, and returns only permitted results. If Graph is unavailable the service returns an error.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User app
  participant S as AI Search
  participant G as Microsoft Graph
  U->>S: Query plus x-ms-query-source-authorization
  S->>G: Resolve groups, including nested
  G-->>S: Membership
  S-->>U: Permitted results only
  G--xS: Unavailable gives 5xx, no partial result

explain.md: Since `2025-11-01-preview`, ACL filters apply even with an API key or admin role, and omitting the token returns only public documents. Earlier previews returned everything, so re-test anything validated on them. To see all documents while debugging, send `x-ms-enable-elevated-read: true` (Search POST only, REST `2026-05-01-preview` or later, needs a role that allows elevated reads) [[r12]]. ACLs list allowed ids only, so there are no deny rules, unlike Graph external item ACLs [[tr14]].

whereToUse: Pilots and internal tools over ADLS Gen2 or Blob data that carries POSIX-like ACLs
Assistants whose users are all Entra identities with nested group memberships
Teams that want the service, not their own code, to expand groups through Graph
Knowledge sources created with ingestionPermissionOptions in agentic retrieval [[r17]]

use: Identities are in Entra and groups nest
A preview with no SLA is acceptable
Allow lists are enough, with no deny rules
avoid: Production workloads that need GA and an SLA
Files with more than 32 ACL entries (ADLS Gen2) or 1,000 (SharePoint)
More than five distinct rbacScope values
flips: GA is required: use security filters and own the group resolution
Revocation must be faster than your sync: push ACL changes or add a live check
Identities are not in Entra: native enforcement does not apply

pitfalls.symptom: Results come back unfiltered for an indexed knowledge source
pitfalls.cause: The source was created without ingestionPermissionOptions, so no permission metadata exists and the header does nothing
pitfalls.fix: Set it at creation and test with a revoked canary user [[r17]]

pitfalls.symptom: A developer with an admin key sees only public documents
pitfalls.cause: Since 2025-11-01-preview ACL filters apply to keys and admin roles, and a missing token returns public documents only
pitfalls.fix: Send the user token, or use elevated read for debugging on Search POST

pitfalls.symptom: Some users miss documents they should see
pitfalls.cause: The source file has more ACL entries than the limit, so some entries are not enforced
pitfalls.fix: Flatten to groups at the source and stay under 32 (ADLS Gen2) or 1,000 (SharePoint)

pitfalls.cause: The index copy of the ACL is stale, since pull indexers run every 5 to 1,440 minutes
pitfalls.fix: Push ACL merges on change, or add a live check for restricted hits [[r19]]

scenarios.title: Internal pilot over a data lake
scenarios.situation: A team pilots an assistant over ADLS Gen2 files with POSIX-like ACLs. Users are in Entra with deeply nested groups. Preview is acceptable for the pilot and hours of revocation lag are fine.
unknowns: Do files stay within 32 ACL entries?
Is the pilot meant to become production?
scenarios.question: How do you enforce access?

options.name: Native ACL filters with the user's token in x-ms-query-source-authorization
options.why: Graph expands nested groups at query time, the service fails closed and you write no group code [[r12]].
options.tradeoff: Preview, no SLA, and an upgrade path to plan.

options.name: Security filters with your own Graph membership code
options.tradeoff: You write and test nested-group expansion and sync.

options.name: Post-filter each hit with a Graph membership call
options.why: A small visible fraction starves top-k and adds a call per hit.
options.tradeoff: Fine when nearly all documents are visible.

flips.if: The pilot must go to production with an SLA
flips.then: Move to security filters or accept the preview risk in writing.

flips.if: Files carry more than 32 ACL entries
flips.then: Flatten groups at the source first.

scenarios.takeaway: Native ACLs suit Entra-based pilots that can tolerate preview.

scenarios.title: Production workload with an SLA
scenarios.situation: A customer-facing assistant goes live in two months. The business demands a GA, supported feature set. Content sits in Blob storage, users are in Entra, and each holds about 50 groups. Revocation within one hour is fine.
unknowns: Is there a rollback if preview behaviour changes?
scenarios.question: Which option do you ship?

options.name: Native ACL filters in production
options.why: They are preview with no SLA and the docs do not recommend them for production [[r11]].
options.tradeoff: A fit for pilots and non-critical tools.

options.name: Security filters with a group list from the token or Graph, ACLs pushed to the index
options.why: GA on any API version, and 50 groups is a small filter [[r13]].
options.tradeoff: You own group resolution and ACL sync.

options.name: Native ACLs behind a feature flag, with a security-filter fallback
options.why: Lets you adopt native ACLs when they reach GA.
options.tradeoff: Two code paths to test, and preview behaviour has already changed (2025-11-01-preview).

flips.then: Re-evaluate: it removes your expansion code.
Compress the filter or use roles.

scenarios.takeaway: An SLA requirement points to the GA pattern.

scenarios.title: More permissions than the limits allow
scenarios.situation: Some files have 60 ACL entries and the corpus has 12 department scopes. The team plans to use ADLS Gen2 ACLs and rbacScope.
unknowns: Can entries be grouped at the source?
Can scopes be modelled as groups?
scenarios.question: What do you change?

options.name: Trust the native ingestion and test later
options.why: Entries beyond 32 might not be enforced and rbacScope allows five distinct values per index [[r15]] [[r12]].
options.tradeoff: Acceptable only if files stay within limits.

options.name: Replace per-user ACL entries with groups at the source, and model departments as groupIds
options.why: Fewer entries per file, and a groupIds field holds up to 1,000 values, so 12 departments fit.
options.tradeoff: Group hygiene work at the source.

options.name: Fall back to security filters with your own expansion
options.why: No native limits, and you control the sync.

flips.then: Use security filters and compute principals yourself.

flips.if: Departments fall to five or fewer

scenarios.takeaway: Check source limits before you commit to native ingestion.

scenarios.title: Revocation within two minutes
scenarios.situation: Security wants a revoked user removed from results within two minutes. Content comes from ADLS Gen2 via an indexer on a schedule, with native ACL fields.
unknowns: Can the source emit change events?
Is a live check on restricted hits acceptable?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: Set the indexer interval to one minute
options.why: The schedule minimum is 5 minutes, so one minute is not available [[r19]].
options.tradeoff: A 5-minute interval fits only targets of five minutes or more.

options.name: Push ACL merges from change events, plus a live check on restricted hits
options.why: Push lets you update userIds or groupIds immediately with merge, and the check covers gaps [[r19]].
options.tradeoff: You own the change feed and the extra call.

options.name: Indexer every 5 minutes and accept the lag
options.tradeoff: Misses two minutes by design, and token and Graph caches add more.

flips.if: Only a few documents are restricted
flips.then: Apply the live check to those only.

scenarios.takeaway: A pull indexer cannot beat its schedule floor.

quiz.q: A developer runs the same query with an admin API key and no user token and sees only a few public documents. On which API versions does this happen and why?
options: Any version: ACLs never apply to keys
Since 2025-11-01-preview: ACL filters apply even with a key, and no token returns only public documents
Only before 2025-11-01-preview, when keys were blocked
Only on stable 2026-04-01, which blocks previews
quiz.explain: From 2025-11-01-preview ACL filters apply to keys and admin roles, and a missing token yields public documents only. Earlier previews returned everything. Elevated read with a header is the debugging path.

quiz.q: Which statements about native ACL enforcement are correct? Choose all that apply.
options: A document passes if any of userIds, groupIds or rbacScope matches
The service falls back to partial results if Microsoft Graph is down
Group membership is resolved through Graph at query time, including nested groups
Deny rules are supported in the ACL fields
quiz.explain: Matching is an OR across the three types, and Graph resolves nested membership. If Graph is down the service returns a 5xx and no partial result, and the fields list allowed ids only.

quiz.q: Order the steps of a native ACL query.
items: The app sends the query with the user's Entra token in x-ms-query-source-authorization
The service checks the calling app has Search Index Data Reader
Graph resolves the user's groups, including nested ones
Documents whose ACL matches the user oid, groups or rbacScope are returned
quiz.explain: The token arrives with the query, the caller role is checked, membership is expanded and only matching documents come back.

flashcards.front: Which header carries the user's token for native ACL queries?
flashcards.back: x-ms-query-source-authorization. For retrieve calls the token scope is https://search.azure.com/.default. Elevated read for debugging uses x-ms-enable-elevated-read.
1,000 values per userIds or groupIds field, five distinct rbacScope values per index, 32 ADLS Gen2 ACL entries and 1,000 SharePoint entries per file.
ACL filters now apply even with an API key or admin role, and a missing user token returns only public documents. Earlier previews returned everything.
No. As of 2026-10-13 it is preview with no SLA. The stable API 2026-04-01 does not include it.
